consensus_summary: Nineveh is the dual symbol of a wicked pagan/Gentile city that repents under Jonah (receiving mercy and serving as Jesus’ exemplar of repentance that will rise to condemn the unrepentant) and of the arrogant bloody empire irreversibly judged in Nahum/Zephaniah; the Jonah/Matthew repentance-mercy strand is the most common primary.
book_summary: A great city of the sea — Gentile people who repent and rise in judgment against those who reject Jesus.
consensus_core_identification: repentant Gentile city/people who receive mercy and will condemn the unrepentant at judgment
book_core_identification: Gentile people who repent and rise in judgment against those who reject Jesus
rationale: Minimum cores are identical: both center on the Jonah/Matt 12:41 identification of Nineveh’s people as repentant Gentiles who function as eschatological witnesses against rejectors of God’s messenger. The book’s ‘city of the sea’ phrasing and silence on the Nahum judgment motif are immaterial wording/emphasis differences that do not alter the shared referent or its primary cases.
strongest_objection: Consensus regularly pairs the repentance motif with equal-weight Nahum judgment symbolism that the book entirely omits, and ‘great city of the sea’ is non-standard.
